newsitem.title: ITALY: S&P raises Cofiri Int'l eurodlr comm paper rating.
newsitem.headline: S&P raises Cofiri Int'l eurodlr comm paper rating.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Monday it has raised to A-2 from A-3 its eurodollar commercial paper programme of Cofiri International Inc., and the short-term issuer rating of parent company and guarantor Compagnia Finanziamenti e Rifinanziamenti SpA (Cofiri SpA).

The upgrade reflects S&P's assessment of sovereign support for obligations of the 100 percent state-owned Istituto per la Ricostruzione Industriale (IRI), the Italian industrial conglomerate of which Cofiri SpA is a wholly-owned subsidiary.
In a statement received in Milan, S&P said Cofiri SpA's issuer rating was based on IRI's credit quality.

"The Italian government has consistently demonstrated commitment to IRI through the last several years, in negotiating an accord with the European Commission in relation to financial relief for the state holding group.

"The original agreement of 1993 (the 'Andreatta-Van Miert' agreement) pertained to a special 10 trillion lire facility advanced by state finance unit Cassa Depositi e Prestiti. This facility is viewed by the government and by European competition authorities as bridging support required in order to allow IRI to proceed with its large-scale privatisation program.

"The extension through mid-1997 of the Andreatta-Van Miert agreement involved the government's transitional purchase in December 1996 of IRI's 61 percent shareholding in the Stet telephone utility. IRI is to receive at least 14.53 trillion lire in reimbursement for this shareholding...

"IRI has thus begun, despite persisting delays in the Stet privatisation, to reduce its considerable debt burden which stood in excess of 20 trillion lire before the transfer of the Stet shareholding," the statement said.
Cofiri SpA and its subsidiaries comprise the main financial arm of the IRI group, which includes Finmeccanica, Alitalia, Societa Autostrade, Rome airports and RAI television.
"Its programme of divestments have caused IRI's national strategic significance and policy role to become less clear, looking forward over the medium and long term.

"However, state support remains the key element underpinning Cofiri's rating, and Standard & Poor's will therefore continue to monitor the rating in light of Italy's dynamic policy environment," the statement concluded.
